newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Medical costs fuel rise in S.African CPI in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Medical costs fuel rise in S.African CPI in Jan.

text.p: The monthly increase of 1.3 percent in January's consumer price index was largely on the back of a rise in the medical care and health expenses category, the Central Statistical Service (CSS) said on Thursday.
The CSS said in a statement medical care and health expenses contributed 0.7 of a percentage point to the monthly 1.3 percent rise -- mainly due to an increase in doctors' and dentists' fees.
The year-on-year rise in CPI was 9.4 percent, the same as for December 1996 and the highest since June 1995 when it stood at 10.0 percent.

Other contributors to the monthly 1.3 percent increase were food (+0.2 of a percentage point), housing (+0.1), fuel and power (+0.1), transport (+0.3), communication (-0.2 due to a 41.6 percent decrease in telephone installation costs) and "other" items (+0.1).
The price index for food showed an annual rate of increase of 8.9 percent in January 1997 -- 1.0 percentage point lower than the corresponding rate of 9.9 percent in December 1996.

The CSS said the monthly rate of increase for food of 0.9 percent was caused by increases in the price indices for fruits and nuts (+4.2 percent), fats and oils (+1.4), meat (+1.0), milk, cheese and eggs (+0.7), vegetables (+0.4), fish and other seafood (+0.3), coffee, tea and cocoa (+0.3), grain products (+0.1) and "other" items (+0.8).
The increases were partially counteracted by a decrease in the price index for sugar (-0.7), the CSS added.
